title: A Mind Does Not Fit in a Feed
centralQuestion: What must happen between first encountering an idea and having the right to say we understood it?
thesis: For complex problems, sustained, structured and active reading deserves protection, not because length cures superficiality but because some thoughts need continuity to be finished.
audienceFit: readers who consume many ideas daily and want evidence-aware ways to turn them into understanding and action
motif: A column of short feed fragments is crossed by one continuous orange thread that gathers them and leaves the column whole.

scenes.title: Full day, unfinished idea
lines: You can meet many ideas in one day and still not say what you understood.
A Mind Does Not Fit in a Feed asks why abundance can leave an idea unfinished.
Its adversary is not the short form, but the impression of understanding.
It defends intellectual continuity: time for a question to develop and face contradiction.

emotionalPlan.arc: recognition rising into a clear, sober claim
emotionalPlan.purpose: Name a familiar paradox, then show what the book argues and what it does not attack.
voiceDirections: Warm and close, as if describing the listener's own evening.
Lift slightly on the question, unhurried.
Clear contrast between the two halves, no sarcasm.
Settled and confident, stress continuity.

scenes.title: Evidence before the verdict
lines: Chapter One calls a fragment's hidden premises and alternatives “context debt,” a working concept.
Chapter Two separates research findings, plausible interpretations and normative recommendations about attention.
Chapter Three holds books to account: padding, false coherence and borrowed authority.

emotionalPlan.arc: analytical tension resolved by fairness
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the method: precise concepts, honest evidence and self-criticism of books.
voiceDirections: Even pace, gentle emphasis on context debt, neutral on the caveat.
Crisp and methodical, small pauses between the three categories.
Slightly wry honesty, firm on the list.

scenes.title: A thought you finish
lines: Chapter Four turns agreement into action: one small, verifiable change, proposed rather than proven.
Chapter Five lets blogs, short explanations and stable editions cooperate instead of compete.
Read it to learn when you have truly earned the words “I understood.”
Begin with the prologue, “A full day, an unfinished idea,” and stay with one question.

emotionalPlan.arc: practical openness easing into a concrete invitation
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show what the reader gains and give a real starting point.
voiceDirections: Encouraging and concrete, honest on the caveat.
Open and constructive, no hostility toward the internet.

Warm and unhurried, a quiet invitation to begin.

title: Affective Calculus
genre: conceptual monograph on affective science and verifiable AI
centralQuestion: Can an AI explain why someone feels an emotion, rather than only naming it from words?
thesis: An emotion is largely an evaluated relationship between an agent and a world that matters to it, so affective labels should follow from a testable appraisal structure checked by counterfactual changes.
audienceFit: readers in AI evaluation, affective science, cognitive modelling and literary interpretation who want emotion judgements that can be explained and falsified
motif: A radial appraisal vector whose shape shifts when one fact changes, moving the dominant point from fear toward anger.

scenes.title: Not just a word
lines: Affective Calculus asks whether an AI can explain an emotion, not merely name it.
A character can say “I’m perfectly fine” in a scene of despair.
An AI judge hunting for emotion words mistakes that expression for the actual state.
The book treats emotion as an evaluated relationship between an agent and its world.

emotionalPlan.arc: curiosity sharpens into recognition of a real problem
emotionalPlan.purpose: Identify the book and why its question matters within the first twenty seconds.
voiceDirections: Open with a confident, curious lift on 'explain'.
Soften; let the quoted words land with gentle irony.
Steady and precise, a slight frown in the voice.
Settle warmly, as a clear definition.

scenes.title: The appraisal vector
lines: Its proposed Appraisal Affective Calculus first separates brief episodes from moods, sentiments and attitudes.
An appraisal vector then records goals, control, agency, norms, dignity and attachment.
Labels become probabilistic prototypes, with intensity and confidence reported separately.

emotionalPlan.arc: careful construction, building a usable instrument step by step
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the method precisely without jargon overload.
voiceDirections: Measured pace; give each category its own small beat.
Slightly brighter, listing dimensions with even rhythm.
Calm and exact, a light emphasis on 'separately'.

scenes.title: Change one fact
lines: Mara faces a running dog, a locked gate and a dead-end alley: fear.
Now she can shut the gate, and the owner freed the dog deliberately: anger should rise.
Such minimal pairs reveal whether an AI explains emotion or only matches words.
Read it for that test, starting with Chapter 1, “An Emotion Is Not a Word.”

emotionalPlan.arc: tension of a concrete scene, a pivot, then a confident invitation
emotionalPlan.purpose: Demonstrate the counterfactual test on the book's own example and give a specific starting point.
voiceDirections: Quicker and tighter, then a short pause before 'fear'.
Shift tone decisively on 'anger', firm but not loud.
Slow down; let the distinction register.
Warm, direct invitation, unhurried on the chapter title.

title: Enthusiasm: The Missing Energy of a Successful Civilization
centralQuestion: Why does a world rich in possibility struggle to turn it into voluntary, meaningful commitment?
thesis: Enthusiasm is voluntary energy directed toward a future one can help shape; institutions can keep safety and reliability while making worthwhile beginnings possible through permission, protected experiments and honest work.
audienceFit: readers who design or work inside schools, companies, research labs and communities, and anyone with ideas but no credible first move
motif: A circuit runs from a small present-world terminal to a larger possible-future terminal, while scattered sparks of stimulation flicker without joining the current.

scenes.title: The missing voltage
lines: Modern systems can run remarkably well without anyone feeling inspired.
This essay asks why a civilization so rich in possibility struggles to commit.
Its answer is enthusiasm: voluntary energy toward a future you can help shape.
Stimulation keeps nudging attention; voltage is the sense that effort moves something worthwhile.

emotionalPlan.arc: calm recognition of a working world rises to the tension of an unanswered question, released by a precise definition
emotionalPlan.purpose: identify the book, its question and its central distinction within the first twenty seconds
voiceDirections: even and observational, slight appreciation

scenes.title: Traps and ignition
lines: The author shows how safeguards, metrics and early evaluation make beginnings costly.
Dreams get judged as credentials or business models before they gain depth.
Ignition needs a reachable first step, visible consequences and enough control to change the work.
The book also confronts cults, bubbles, burnout and the unpaid passion tax.

voiceDirections: steady, explanatory pace
slight weight on 'before they gain depth'
brighter, listing each condition clearly

scenes.title: Permission to begin
lines: It proposes protected experiments, honest work and communities with room for dissent.
Even generative AI is weighed: who still chooses, checks and stays with the result?
If your ideas lack a credible first move, begin with “The Missing Voltage.”

title: Incomplete Tribes
centralQuestion: Can a peaceful civilization be built without first requiring humanity to become morally good?
thesis: Deep cooperation needs bounded groups, so belonging should be redesigned as incomplete tribes: communities strong enough to shape a life but constitutionally limited so that none owns a person or treats outsiders as expendable, linked in a polycentric order where conflicts stay survivable.
audienceFit: readers weighing polarization, identity, institutional design and the social pressures of artificial intelligence
motif: An archipelago of distinct islands of different sizes, joined by several bridges so that no single island becomes the whole world.

scenes.title: Good People First?
lines: Incomplete Tribes is an essay on a dangerous question: must humanity become good before civilization works?
Its answer is architectural: change the design of belonging, not human nature.
We love, build and mourn in groups, yet loyalty can turn neighbours into enemies.

emotionalPlan.arc: provocation to recognition
emotionalPlan.purpose: Name the book, its unsettling question and why belonging must be redesigned rather than abolished.
voiceDirections: Name the book plainly, then pose the question for real, lifting on 'good before'.
Steady and clear; lean on 'architectural'.
Warm on the first half, quieter and graver on 'enemies'.

scenes.title: Deep, Never Total
lines: Chapter Nine defines an incomplete tribe: thick cooperation without total authority over members.
A chess club may govern tournament conduct, but not a member's romantic life.
Other loyalties count as safeguards, so no group becomes the sole source of truth and affection.
Exit and dissent stay open, so disagreement is not treated as betrayal.

emotionalPlan.arc: definition to concrete reassurance
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the book's method: constitutional limits on groups, made tangible through its own examples.
voiceDirections: Measured, definitional; small pause after the colon.
Lightly wry, let the example land.
Build gently toward 'truth and affection'.
Settle down; reassuring and unhurried.

scenes.title: Bridges, Not Walls
lines: Overlapping loyalties make people harder to sort into clean enemy camps.
Peace becomes an institution that lets rivals lose without being erased.
Chapter Fifteen tests it against AI that could become the sole interpreter of a member's world.
Start with the Prelude, The Question Beneath the Question, and find hope without an ideal human.

emotionalPlan.arc: insight to tested hope to invitation
emotionalPlan.purpose: Deliver what readers gain, show the idea under modern pressure and end with a concrete starting point.
voiceDirections: Clear and quietly pleased with the insight.
Firm on 'institution', softer on 'without being erased'.
Slightly faster and more urgent, then ease at the end.
Warm and direct; speak the chapter title as a title.

title: Is There Light at the End of the Tunnel?
centralQuestion: Why do systems built to liberate people so often rebuild the dependencies they opposed, and can institutions be designed to correct that?
thesis: No doctrine guarantees a just order; the realistic light is a civilization whose institutions obstruct domination, keep exit and challenge open, and turn errors into correction.
audienceFit: readers who distrust both nostalgia and apologetics and want a careful, evidence-graded look at power, freedom, markets, democracy and AI
motif: Nested tunnel arches narrow toward a small warm opening, where light stands for institutions that can still be challenged and corrected.

scenes.title: When the exit resembles the entrance
lines: This political essay begins with an unease: systems promising freedom rebuild the dependencies they opposed.
Equality can conceal a caste, and economic freedom can buy political power.
The initiator's experience of communism serves as testimony and a source of questions, not proof.

emotionalPlan.arc: unease deepening into sober gravity
emotionalPlan.purpose: Name the book's recurring danger and promise within the first thirty seconds.
voiceDirections: Plain and arresting; let 'rebuild' carry the unease.
Lower and slower; give each paradox its own beat.
Steady and honest; underline 'not proof' calmly.

scenes.title: Power changes its costume
lines: Its real question is architectural: who can compel whom, and who can replace them?
Privilege lives in office, careers, information and status, and each can convert into another.
When winners can rewrite the rules, market reward becomes political power.
Cited findings, possible mechanisms and working proposals stay apart, so you can weigh the evidence.

emotionalPlan.arc: from analytic focus through tension to clarity
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the method: architectural questions, convertible privilege, graded evidence.
voiceDirections: Crisp and curious; slight pause before the two questions.
Even pace through the list, a small stress on 'convert'.
Firmer and slower, a hint of warning.
Release the tension; plain, reassuring precision.

scenes.title: A constitution open to correction
lines: It proposes constitutional cosmolocalism: global knowledge, distributed capacities, and rights beyond local goodwill.
Artificial intelligence and basic income are tested by who owns, who controls, and who speaks.
Its light is modest: institutions where errors become information and leaders can be replaced peacefully.
Start with the introduction, When the Exit Resembles the Entrance, then test the ten clauses yourself.

emotionalPlan.arc: constructive proposal to a personal, open invitation
emotionalPlan.purpose: Present the proposal and its test, then give a concrete starting point.
voiceDirections: Clear and deliberate; enunciate 'cosmolocalism' without rushing.
Even, questioning tone; stress the three tests lightly.
Slow, earnest, close to the listener; let 'modest' sound like strength.
Warm and direct, like handing over the book.

title: The Messiah Factory
subtitle: Why We Confuse the Power to Persuade with the Capacity to Understand
genre: social philosophy and epistemology of authority
centralQuestion: Why do the qualities that build an audience get mistaken for the capacity to understand, and how can influence stay correctable?
thesis: When rewards for securing allegiance arrive sooner than rewards for being correct, groups may select for voices that stabilize belief over those that improve it; the book proposes separated roles, staged evaluation and 'incomplete tribes' so cooperation can survive correction.
audienceFit: readers interested in leadership, charisma, online attention, group belief, institutional design and how communities can admit error
motif: A crowd of small audience dots feeds a rising beam that inflates a halo above a single podium, while a deliberate gap left open in the halo marks room for correction.

scenes.title: Who gets heard
lines: The Messiah Factory asks why the power to persuade keeps passing for understanding.
Its suspicion is that becoming audible may reward fixed answers over revisable thought.
Yet the book also refuses the flattering story of the ignored genius.
Its real subject is how coordinating a group becomes control over what it may question.

emotionalPlan.arc: curiosity sharpens into an uneasy recognition, then steadies into fair-minded inquiry
emotionalPlan.purpose: Name the book, its hook and why it deserves attention within the first twenty seconds.
voiceDirections: Open warmly with a hint of challenge, light stress on 'passing for understanding'.
Lower slightly, thoughtful, as if sharing a private suspicion.
Turn with a small, honest 'yet', fair and unhurried.
Settle into clear, grounded emphasis on 'what it may question'.

scenes.title: Audiences make prophets
lines: It first separates attention, credibility, authority, performance and welfare into different contests.
Audiences reward some versions of a speaker until that persona becomes the speaker's livelihood.
The danger begins when no evidence can genuinely reduce the center's authority.

emotionalPlan.arc: precise analysis builds tension as the feedback loop closes
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the book's method: distinguishing contests and tracing the leader-audience relationship.
voiceDirections: Measured and clear, giving each of the five contests its own beat.
Slightly slower, observant, letting 'livelihood' land.
Quiet and firm, a grave weight on 'no evidence' without drama.

scenes.title: Cooperation without prophets
lines: Its proposed discovery system weighs claims rather than names, and must never become an oracle.
Its incomplete tribes offer real shared work while protecting disagreement, outside ties and departure.
Read it to learn how commitment can survive correction without waiting for a messiah.
Begin with “Who Gets Heard,” and ask which contest your trusted voices won.

emotionalPlan.arc: tension releases into constructive hope and a direct, personal invitation
emotionalPlan.purpose: Present the book's proposals honestly as proposals, give a specific reason to read and a real starting chapter.
voiceDirections: Careful and precise, a slight caution on 'never become an oracle'.

Lift gently, sincere invitation, light stress on 'survive correction'.
Close and conversational, a small smile on the final question.

title: The New Social Contract in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
centralQuestion: If artificial intelligence makes production far less dependent on human labour, how can people keep rights and bargaining power instead of becoming comfortable dependants?
thesis: Broad delegation to automated institutions is justified only while it stays revocable and accompanied by effective rights of oversight, contestation, replacement and exit, set out as twenty-one debatable clauses.
audienceFit: readers interested in AI governance, political philosophy, constitutional design and the distribution of automation gains
motif: A gold automated hub radiates services to independent nodes, each still connected by a link it can contest, cut or reroute.

scenes.title: Comfort without surrender
lines: Imagine an automated order offering comfort, safety and varied experiences, if you hand it governance.
This book takes that offer seriously, answering with twenty-one debatable clauses of a new social contract.
Its fear is not scarcity, but a leadership that controls automated infrastructure and cannot be replaced.

emotionalPlan.arc: Curiosity at a tempting offer, sharpening into concern about irreplaceable control.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Identify the book, its central offer and why it deserves attention within the first thirty seconds.
voiceDirections: Open warmly, as if presenting a genuine invitation.
Firm and clear; land on twenty-one clauses.
Lower and more serious; stress cannot be replaced.

scenes.title: Delegate, never surrender
lines: Administration may be delegated to automated systems, but collective goals must stay under legitimate control.
A right to leave a provider counts only if identity, records and services move too.
An appeal needs reasons, corrected facts, independent review and a real remedy.
Those who set goals, run infrastructure and oversee rights must remain separate powers.

emotionalPlan.arc: Steady construction of safeguards, each one adding firmness.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the book's method: concrete institutional conditions that keep delegation revocable.
voiceDirections: Measured; contrast delegated with must stay.
Practical, with a slight emphasis on move too.
Crisp, giving each requirement its own beat.
Confident and even, closing the argument.

scenes.title: Clauses under stress
lines: Later clauses protect attention, privacy, ecological budgets, reproductive freedom and room for new generations.
The final chapters ask who pays, who enforces, and why powerful actors would comply.
Its test is clear: abundance is legitimate when it reduces dependency, not when it makes dependency comfortable.
Begin with the Introduction, where the book sets out the political offer of an automated order.

emotionalPlan.arc: Widening scope, then a probing challenge, a clear verdict, and a warm invitation to read.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Preview the clauses, state the book's test of legitimate abundance, and give a real starting point.
voiceDirections: Flowing and open, letting the list breathe.
Pointed, with a small pause before comply.
Clear and weighted; contrast reduces with comfortable.
Warm and unhurried, a direct invitation.

title: The Unfinished World
subtitle: Why the Future Is Still Worth Wanting
centralQuestion: How can hope stay serious when the future looks small and nothing is guaranteed?
thesis: Hope is a commitment to a possible good under uncertainty: the world is unfinished, and its open frontiers, companions and institutions leave places where effort can still matter.
audienceFit: readers tired of both hype and cynicism who want a rigorous, non-naive reason to act on the future
motif: A dark half-mapped globe at dawn, some surface tiles filled and others still dashed and open, shows the epilogue's image of reality having seams where effort can enter.

scenes.title: A future grown small
lines: The Unfinished World opens with a strange diagnosis: our future has begun to look small.
We inherited machines that edit genes and reach other worlds, yet our mood is often fatigue.
This book argues for hope without denying climate risk, war, or concentrated power.
Its starting fact is simple: almost everything we care about is still unfinished.

emotionalPlan.arc: Recognition of a quiet cultural weariness rises into the surprising claim that the world is still open.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Identify the book, its diagnosis and why it deserves attention within the first thirty seconds.
voiceDirections: Curious and clear, lean slightly on 'small'.
Light irony, contrast the achievements with the tired ending.
Steady and serious, no drama on the list of dangers.
Warm lift, let 'unfinished' land with a short pause.

scenes.title: Hope without prophecy
lines: Here hope is not prediction; it is commitment to a possible good under uncertainty.
It asks whether an outcome is possible, valuable and influenceable enough to justify action.
Awe widens the horizon, agency finds a lever, and fellowship makes effort endurable.

emotionalPlan.arc: From a precise redefinition through a practical test to the human mechanics that sustain effort.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show how the book rebuilds hope as a disciplined, non-naive stance.
voiceDirections: Precise and calm, separate 'prediction' from 'commitment'.
Measured, give each of the three criteria its own beat.
Building warmth across the three clauses, natural pace.

scenes.title: Reality has seams
lines: Its frontiers run from an unmapped mind to a universe that is still mostly night.
Courage becomes rational when institutions make intelligent failure survivable.
Read it for a hope that survives tragedy because it never promised an ending.
Begin with the prologue, We Are Too Early to Give Up, and choose a frontier.

emotionalPlan.arc: Wonder at the open frontiers grounds itself in institutions, then settles into a personal, quiet invitation.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Present selected content, give a specific reason to read and a real starting point.
voiceDirections: Expansive and unhurried, a slight lift on 'mostly night'.
Firm and practical, stress 'survivable'.
Sincere and personal, slower on the final clause.
Soft and direct, say the prologue title as a title.

title: Two Ways to Build a World
genre: political philosophy and social science essay
centralQuestion: What remains of the partnership-domination idea when we refuse to romanticize the past?
thesis: Domination and partnership are recurrent coordination equilibria; technology and institutions change their relative cost without abolishing either repertoire.
audienceFit: readers interested in power, cooperation, institutional design, and how AI may reshape who can coordinate whom
motif: A stepped rust pyramid stands beside a teal lattice of linked nodes, two buildable architectures of coordination taken from the book's cover.

scenes.title: After the golden age
lines: A nearly forty-year-old idea claims societies keep organizing around partnership or domination.
Two Ways to Build a World keeps Riane Eisler's contrast and drops the peaceful golden age.
It treats domination and partnership as two recurring ways people coordinate under power.
Its central claim is that technology and institutions change which way is cheaper.

emotionalPlan.arc: recognition of an old contested idea, then clarity about what the book rescues and why it matters now
emotionalPlan.purpose: Identify the book, its honest correction of the myth, and its central claim within twenty-five seconds.
voiceDirections: Open with quiet weight, let 'partnership or domination' land as the stakes.
Plain and fair, a small turn on 'drops'.
Steady and explanatory, stress 'coordinate'.
Lean in slightly on 'technology and institutions' and 'cheaper'.

scenes.title: From boxes to coordinates
lines: Instead of labelling whole civilizations, the book measures relationships along distinct dimensions.
It asks who can leave, speak, appeal, observe decisions, and impose sanctions.
Domination appears when wealth, media, office, and force convert into each other until escape disappears.
Hierarchy can stay legitimate when its purpose, scope, duration, review, and exit are clear.

emotionalPlan.arc: analytical build from method to the warning about closing loops, released by a constructive distinction
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the book's method: a coordinate system of concrete questions, the danger of convertible status, and hierarchy without domination.
voiceDirections: Measured and clear, as if laying out a map.

scenes.title: Partnership needs teeth
lines: Drawing on commons governance, it shows cooperation needs boundaries, monitoring, graduated sanctions, and appeal.
Artificial intelligence can become an empire machine, or it can lower the cost of partnership.
Start with Chapter 3, From Binary to Coordinate System, and learn to map who holds power.

emotionalPlan.arc: practical firmness, a sharp present-day stake, then an inviting concrete starting point
emotionalPlan.purpose: Deliver the book's design lessons and its AI stakes, and give the reader a specific place to begin.
voiceDirections: Grounded and practical, no sermon.
Contrast the two halves, slight pause before 'or'.
Friendly and direct, name the chapter clearly, warm lift on 'who holds power'.

title: We Manufacture Our Own Masters
centralQuestion: How do institutions built for freedom become instruments of domination, and how can people keep the power to refuse?
thesis: The mechanism through which a political ideal succeeds can produce its opposite, so free orders must be judged under hostile leadership and protected by testable counterpowers rather than goodwill.
audienceFit: readers of political philosophy, institutional design and technology policy who distrust both utopias and easy cynicism
motif: A stepped pedestal built from ordinary blocks raises a crown, while one small figure stands apart beside an open gap: the masters we build and the capacity to refuse them.

scenes.title: Ideals that breed masters
lines: Confiscate every fortune, and someone still decides who gets a home and who may leave.
We Manufacture Our Own Masters calls these traps antinomies, and finds them in every camp.
The author knew them from communism, where levelled incomes still hid a nobility without titles.

emotionalPlan.arc: A concrete provocation rises into a named problem, then grounds itself in personal history.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Establish within thirty seconds what the book is, why it exists and why it matters.
voiceDirections: Quiet and concrete, let the second clause land.
State the title plainly; stress every camp.
Slower and grave, without melodrama.

scenes.title: The hostile-ruler test
lines: Its test is adversarial: judge each system by what a hostile leader could do.
Then ask how the people affected could stop that leader.
Liberalism, Chinese order, private cities and guaranteed income all face the same scrutiny.
Appendices separate supported claims from hypothesis, and the book turns its test on itself.

emotionalPlan.arc: Tension builds as the method is applied evenly to every camp, then releases into intellectual honesty.
emotionalPlan.purpose: Show the book's distinctive method and its fairness across political positions.
voiceDirections: Firm and measured, stress hostile.
Brief pause before stop, then direct.
Steady listing pace, no favourites.
Warmer, reassuring honesty.

scenes.title: Building the power to refuse
lines: Markets can let winners close entry, and floods of noise can silence speech without censors.
Artificial intelligence may cheapen expertise while handing power to whoever owns the infrastructure.
A free order, the book argues, is measured by what citizens can refuse without starving.
Begin with chapter one, Antinomies Are Not Accidents, and run its test on your favourite system.

emotionalPlan.purpose: Give selected content, the essential message and a specific starting point for reading.
